LunaPilot helps plan Moon south pole landings: for Artemis III candidate regions it uses NASA JPL data to compute Sun and Earth elevation, then power and communication scores, a season view and a best-window finder. Our geometry matches NASA JPL Horizons to 0.000 degrees. Live app: https://lunapilot-28tiyt7dwmst4pknnzkqzp.streamlit.app/
summary: LunaPilot is a web app that helps mission planners choose where and when to land near the Moon's south pole. For three Artemis III candidate regions it uses NASA JPL ephemerides to compute the Sun and Earth elevation at the site, then turns this into a power score (share of time the Sun is above the horizon), a communication score (share of time the Earth is visible) and an overall score. Users can compare sites, see a season view, find the best window of the year, and test terrain what-ifs with horizon masks. Our geometry matches NASA JPL Horizons to 0.000 degrees on all three sites in our checks.
details:
LunaPilot is a web app for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. Landing near the lunar south pole is difficult because the Sun stays very close to the horizon and the Earth is only sometimes visible, so power and communication depend strongly on the site and the date.

What it does: for a chosen landing site and date range, LunaPilot computes the Sun and Earth elevation as seen from the site, then derives a power score (share of time the Sun is above the horizon), a comms score (share of time the Earth is above the horizon), an overall score with an adjustable weight, and the longest dark period.

Features: an Explorer tab with elevation charts and metrics; a Compare tab for several sites side by side; a season view that shows month by month changes through a year; a mission window finder that searches a full year for the best run of consecutive days; horizon mask sliders for terrain or antenna what-if tests; and a rule-based Copilot that answers questions using numbers from our engine.

How it works: our engine uses Skyfield with NASA JPL / NAIF kernels (DE421 ephemeris and lunar orientation data) to compute Sun and Earth directions in the Moon body frame at each site, for dates from 1900 to 2050.

Validation: we compared Sun and Earth elevations from our engine with NASA JPL Horizons for all three sites over 24 hours on 2029-07-01. The maximum difference was 0.000 degrees for both bodies. The log is in docs/horizons_validation.txt in our repository, and the score logic has unit tests.

Scope: the default horizon is flat, so scores can read 0% or 100% near the pole. The mask sliders show how results change if terrain raises the horizon, but they are not measured terrain. Measured LOLA terrain horizons are our next step.

Code: https://github.com/ailanasirai/lunapilot

Team: Aila Nasir (lead, app and product), Ekeu David (engine), Umar Akhtar (team member).
